display.title: Display
display.why.asked: DEVPIT_GDK_BACKEND chose it for this start.
display.why.inherited: GDK_BACKEND was set by whatever started devpit.
display.why.noWayland: This session has no Wayland compositor.
display.why.knownCrash: This desktop's GTK settings crash devpit on Wayland, so it is on X11.
display.why.failedBefore: A Wayland start of this version never loaded its window, so it stays on X11.
display.why.default: Wayland where the desktop has it, X11 where it does not.
display.nextStart: A change applies at the next start.
display.more: DEVPIT_GDK_BACKEND=wayland or x11 overrides this for one start. A Wayland start that never loads its window keeps that version on X11 until a choice is made here.
language.title: Language
language.said: devpit's own words follow this choice, without a restart.
theme.title: Theme
settings.account.stays: Projects, boards, conversations, terminal history and files stay on this computer.
settings.account.signOutSaid: Clears the signed-in state on this computer
settings.projects.note: Removing a project takes it out of devpit. The folder, the git repository and your code are never touched — devpit only forgets where it was.
settings.storage.directorySaid: Each project gets one, holding its board, skills, capabilities, transcripts and worktrees. None of it is in the repository.
settings.storage.note: Transcripts are always written: a session that a restart loses is a session that was never yours to come back to. Nothing is uploaded, and removing a project leaves its folder where it is.
settings.appearance.terminalNote: The terminal keeps its dark ground in every theme. A shell paints its own ANSI colours for a dark background; on a white one they stop being readable.
about.privacySaid: What devpit keeps on this computer and what it ever sends.
about.licenceSaid: devpit is open source, under the Apache License 2.0.
about.noticesSaid: The notices of the work devpit includes.
archive.note: Conversations of {name} you archived from their menu. Restoring one puts it back in the lists.
pause.title: Pause
pause.said: Quiet for a meeting or a stretch of thought. Agents keep working.
pause.more: No notifications, the island neither opens nor sounds, and a terminal’s permission question goes straight to that terminal. Agents’ news is still heard and reminders still go off. Also in the status strip and the tray.
pause.resumeTitle: Resume: notifications, the island and its questions come back
onboarding.changeLater: You can change it later in Settings.
onboarding.projectSaid: A folder with a git repository in it. devpit reads it where it is and never moves it.
onboarding.browserCheck: . Check that it shows this code, then approve it there — this screen moves on by itself.
onboarding.signInTitle: Sign in, if you want to
onboarding.freeSaid: Free, and optional. It signs you in; sync between your computers is off until you turn it on, and carries only preferences and project settings, sealed so devpit.app cannot read them.
onboarding.stays: Your projects, conversations and files stay on this computer
profile.name: Name
profile.placeholder.name: GLM
profile.plainProgram: {command} starts no agent devpit knows, so it will be run as a program.
profile.read: Runs {agent}{args}{vars}. It works in the chat and on the board too, not only in a terminal.
profile.commandSaid: What you type in a terminal to start it — an agent such as claude, or a function of your own such as claude-work. devpit reads what it sets.
profile.details: Details — agent, program, arguments and variables
profile.footnote: The program runs with these variables set and these arguments added. Leave Program empty to use {launch}’s own.
profile.footnoteAgent: The program runs with these variables set and these arguments added. Leave Program empty to use the agent’s own.
models.title: Models
models.said: A model switched off leaves the model picker. Add your own in the profile’s models field.
models.defaultModelSaid: What this profile’s chats run when none is picked. Empty leaves it to the CLI.
models.defaultEffortSaid: The effort its chats start with, where the CLI has one. Empty keeps the CLI’s own.
models.advisorSaid: Written as advisorModel into the settings devpit starts this profile’s sessions with, never into the profile’s own settings. Empty is none.
models.subagentSaid: {variable} for this profile’s sessions. Saved with the profile.
waiting.arrived: came from another computer. Look it over below before it runs here.
waiting.needs: came from another computer and needs {needs} here before it can start. Edit it below to fill it in.
waiting.changed: {label}’s {name} was changed on another computer to {value}.
checks.title: Check sign-ins and MCP servers
checks.said: How often the footer looks again while the window is on screen.
checks.every: Check sign-ins and MCP servers every
scan.openFirst: Open a project first: the sign-in runs in one of its terminals.
scan.said: The CLIs devpit holds a chat with, found on your PATH and in the usual install folders. Each one signs in with its own login, in a terminal.
providers.defaultSaid: What a new terminal opens. A plain shell is an answer too.
providers.lost: The default is not on this machine any more, so a new terminal opens a shell.
providers.hooksSaid: Shows working, waiting and done on the island, in the sidebar and on a card.
providers.hooksMore: For Claude Code and the Gemini CLI run in devpit’s terminals. The hooks travel with the launch — nothing is written into your own configuration, so turning this off is the whole of turning it off. Any other agent can report with {command}, run in one of devpit’s terminals.
providers.trustTitle: Trust the folders of the projects I add
providers.trustSaid: Claude Code stops asking whether to trust a project’s folder or its worktrees.
providers.trustMore: Adding a project is the answer: devpit writes it into each Claude Code account it knows, when the project is added and when a worktree is made. A trusted folder’s own {settings} settings — hooks, permissions — apply without asking, so add only what you would trust by hand. Off, the question comes back for new folders.
providers.installedSaid: devpit drives agent CLIs installed on this computer. Open one to change the program it runs, the arguments it carries or the variables it starts with.
providers.newSaid: Another account or endpoint of the same CLI — a second sign-in in its own config directory, or a gateway such as z.ai — is a profile. Each one shows up in the chat’s model picker with its own history, skills and MCP servers.
providers.noneFound: No agent CLI found. devpit looked on your login shell’s PATH and the usual install folders; set a profile’s Command to the full path.
providers.elsewhereSaid: devpit can drive these too. Install one with its own CLI and press Refresh.
remote.risk: Anyone with a paired device can see the terminals on this machine — and, if you allow that device, type in them and answer for you.
remote.title: Remote
remote.said: Reach this machine from your phone or another computer: over your Tailscale tailnet, or from anywhere through devpit.app, encrypted end to end. {risk}
remote.tailscaleTip: Over your tailnet, served by this machine
remote.relayTip: From anywhere, through devpit.app, which cannot read what passes
remote.tailnetStep1: Install Tailscale on the phone or computer and sign in as the owner of this machine{login}. Anyone else in the tailnet is refused.
remote.tailnetStep2: Open this machine’s address on that device.
remote.tailnetStep3: {pair} here, then scan the code or type it there. It is good once, for ten minutes.
remote.tailnetStep4: Choose what the device may do. Watching is always allowed; “type” sends keys to terminals and moves cards; “answer” allows or denies a question an agent is waiting on. Chats are read there, not written.
remote.tailnetNote: The status strip says {watched} while one is connected, and a click drops it. Who connected and what they did, never what was on screen, is kept in {log}.
remote.relayStep1: Sign in to your devpit account on this machine (Settings → Account), and at devpit.app on the device — the same account.
remote.relayStep2: {pair} here and scan the code with its camera. It opens devpit.app/remote with this machine’s key and a secret good once, for ten minutes.
remote.relayStep3: Choose what the device may do. Watching is always allowed; “type” sends keys to terminals and moves cards; “answer” allows or denies a question an agent is waiting on.
remote.relayStep4: {forget} a device here and it is cut off at once: its connection ends, and its key opens nothing after.
remote.relayNote: devpit.app joins the device to this machine and passes along what they say, sealed between the two of them with keys it never holds. The page the device opens comes from devpit.app, so this way you also trust that site’s code; Tailscale does not ask that. The protocol is in {doc}.
remote.installTailscale: Install Tailscale on this machine and on your devices — or choose the devpit.app relay, which needs neither.
remote.loginTailscale: Log in to Tailscale on this machine.
remote.noHttps: Reached over your tailnet’s own encryption. Turn on HTTPS certificates in the tailnet’s admin for an https address.
remote.signInFirst: Sign in to your devpit account first (Settings → Account): devpit.app knows this machine by it.
remote.connected: Connected to devpit.app. A paired device opens devpit.app/remote, signed in to the same account.
remote.scanRelay: Scan it with the device’s camera, or open the link there.
remote.scanTailnet: Scan it, or open the address and type
remote.goodOnce: Good once, for ten minutes. You allow the device here before it pairs.
remote.openOnTailnet: Open it on a device in your tailnet{login}.
remote.noActivity: Nothing done from a device yet.
remote.needsHttps: Adding it to devpit.app/remote needs the tailnet’s HTTPS address.
remote.addToAppTip: Opens devpit.app/remote with this machine’s address; nothing else is sent
remote.asks: {name} asks to pair with this machine
remote.pairedRelay: Paired through devpit.app, known by its key
remote.typeTip: Send keys to terminals and move cards
remote.answerTip: Allow or deny a question an agent is waiting on
remoteMcp.limit: claude.ai and the Claude app cannot connect to it directly: they would have to hold the key that ends the encryption, so they stay out until a way keeps it end to end. Use an MCP client on a computer, such as Claude Code, through devpit there.
remoteMcp.title: Allow remote MCP (read-only)
remoteMcp.said: An MCP client on another computer reads devpit here — the board, the sessions, what waits on you — through devpit.app, encrypted end to end. It changes nothing.
remoteMcp.step1: On the other computer, install devpit and sign in to the same devpit account — or let the pairing command sign it in.
remoteMcp.step2: {pair} here and run the command it shows there. The link in it is good once, for ten minutes; the key it makes stays in that computer’s devpit folder, readable by its user alone.
remoteMcp.step3: Add {command} to the MCP client there, for example {example}.
remoteMcp.step4: {forget} a client here, or turn this off, and it is cut off at once.
remoteMcp.note: It answers reads alone: the projects, their boards and cards, the sessions running and what waits on you. Allowing a tool, answering a session or moving a card stays on this computer or in the Remote. The protocol is in {doc}.
remoteMcp.runThis: Run this on the other computer:
remoteMcp.clientTip: An MCP client, paired through devpit.app and known by its key

secrets.said: Kept in {file}, readable by you alone and kept out of git. Paste a key here, never in a chat: a chat keeps it in its transcript.
secrets.name: Name
secrets.kept: {name} is kept. A session reads it by that name.
secrets.reminds: devpit reminds you to rotate {secret}, on the board.
